skill.name: asana-automation
skill.description: Guides Asana automation through Rube MCP, including setup, OAuth checks, task workflows, projects, sections, users, and pagination.
skill.summary: Use Rube MCP to manage Asana tasks, projects, sections, teams, users, and workspace IDs.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown formatting, Rube MCP tool names, Asana parameter names, and Asana GID references. One low network finding remains because the skill asks users to configure the external Rube MCP endpoint. No prompt injection, covert data exfiltration, or host reconnaissance intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Disclose that Rube MCP is a third-party service and tell users to review OAuth scopes before connecting Asana.
Ask users to confirm workspace, project, task, and section IDs before creating or moving Asana records.
Require a preview step for bulk actions and warn that failed requests do not roll back successful requests.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Asana connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `asana`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
- `projects`: Array of project GIDs to add task to
1. `ASANA_SUBMIT_PARALLEL_REQUESTS` - Execute multiple API calls in parallel [Required]
- `actions`: Array of action objects with method, path, and data
- Asana uses cursor-based pagination with `offset` parameter
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- Each action must be a valid Asana API call

content.user_title: Automate Asana Workflows with Rube MCP
content.value_statement: Asana automation can fail when agents use stale tool schemas or unclear workspace IDs. This skill guides Rube MCP setup, ID resolution, and safe task or project workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides Rube MCP setup and Asana OAuth connection checks.
Instructs agents to search current Rube tool schemas before acting.
Covers task search, creation, detail lookup, subtasks, and due dates.
Covers project, section, and task section management.
Covers workspace teams, team users, workspace users, and current user lookup.
Explains cursor pagination and parallel Asana request handling.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP availability and an active Asana connection.
Depends on current Rube tool schemas, so exact arguments can change.
Parallel requests can leave partial success because rollback is not guaranteed.
Does not provide custom code, local scripts, or direct Asana API calls.

use_cases.title: Create Project Tasks
use_cases.description: Build tasks and subtasks in the correct workspace and project after resolving required Asana IDs.

use_cases.title: Organize Project Sections
use_cases.description: List sections, create missing sections, and move tasks into the right project structure.

use_cases.title: Audit Teams and Users
use_cases.description: List workspace teams, team members, users, and the authenticated Asana account before assignments.

prompt_templates.title: List My Workspaces
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Asana automation skill to find available workspaces through Rube MCP. Show workspace names and GIDs before any changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Project Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Search current schemas, resolve my workspace and project, then create a task with this name, assignee, notes, and due date. Confirm the target project first.

prompt_templates.title: Move Tasks Into Sections
prompt_templates.prompt: Find sections in the selected project, create the requested section if missing, and move the chosen tasks into it. Show exact GIDs before writing.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Bulk Asana Updates
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a reviewed plan for multiple Asana updates using parallel requests. Validate every action, explain partial failure risk, then ask before execution.

output_examples.input: Create an Asana task for the launch checklist due Friday.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies the workspace and project, confirms the target, then reports the created task name, assignee, due date, and Asana link.

output_examples.input: Organize selected tasks into a new QA section.
output_examples.output: The assistant lists the selected project, creates the section if needed, moves the chosen tasks, and notes any tasks that failed.

output_examples.input: List users in the design workspace.
output_examples.output: The assistant resolves the workspace, retrieves users through Rube MCP, and returns names, emails when available, and relevant GIDs.

best_practices: Search Rube tool schemas before every workflow because parameters can change.
Resolve and confirm workspace, project, task, and section GIDs before write operations.
Use parallel requests only after reviewing each action and accepting partial success risk.
anti_patterns: Creating tasks before confirming the workspace and project.
Assuming old tool arguments without checking current schemas.
Using bulk operations when each step needs rollback or strict ordering.

faq.question: Does this skill connect directly to Asana?
faq.answer: No. It guides the agent to use Asana through Rube MCP and Composio.

faq.question: Does it need an Asana OAuth connection?
faq.answer: Yes. Rube must show an active Asana connection before workflows run.

faq.question: Can it create and update tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers task creation, search, details, subtasks, sections, and project assignment through available Rube tools.

faq.question: Can it handle pagination?
faq.answer: Yes. It reminds the agent to use cursor offsets from next page responses.

faq.question: Can it manage teams and users?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes workflows for workspace teams, team members, workspace users, and current user lookup.

faq.question: Are bulk operations transactional?
faq.answer: No. The skill notes that failed individual requests do not roll back successful requests.
